content:
Many people have complained in recent years that Apple's design has lost some of its signature quirky style. The good news is that the latest example seems to tell you things are changing.

Inside the Settings app of iOS 27, Apple has hidden an Easter egg paying tribute to classic Mac OS — the Clarus Dogcow. Here's how to trigger it…

iOS 27 adds a new feature that lets users customise the intensity of the Liquid Glass transparency effect, with a slider ranging from "Clear" to "Tinted". You can find this option on your iPhone via Settings → Appearance → Liquid Glass.

On this screen, Apple has designed a web-like interface that lets you preview how the Liquid Glass appearance changes as you adjust the slider. There's a small scrollable area containing some text and photos of Apple Park.

Here's the Easter egg: scroll all the way to the bottom of the screen, then keep pulling up with your finger, and a photo of a Clarus Dogcow figurine will appear next to the Apple Park pond. Rainbow text reading "Moof!" (the dogcow's call) will also show up in the sample search text field.

If you say "Moof!" to Siri in Spotlight, Siri will reply with "Nice dogcow."

For those unfamiliar with this piece of history, the Clarus Dogcow actually originated as an icon designed by Susan Kare for the original Mac, used as a character in the Cairo font (the classic Mac's icon font, similar to Windows' Dingbats). It basically serves no practical purpose — it's purely a bit of fun.

You can also find the same Easter egg in the Appearance menu of the System Settings app on macOS Golden Gate.
